html:
The Mississippi is the main river of North America, about 3,700 km from Lake Itasca in Minnesota to the Gulf of Mexico below New Orleans. With the Missouri and the Ohio it drains about two fifths of the United States.

Its valley was a heartland of Native North America. At Poverty Point in Louisiana people raised great earthworks more than 3,000 years ago. The Marksville culture of the lower valley built mounds in the early centuries CE, and after about 1050 the maize-growing towns of the Mississippian culture spread along it, with Cahokia near today's St. Louis. Peoples such as the Chitimacha and the Natchez lived on the lower river when Europeans came.

La Salle canoed to its mouth in 1682 and claimed the whole basin for France as Louisiana. Spain held the west bank as Luisiana from 1762, and the United States bought it in the Louisiana Purchase of 1803. Steamboats then made the river the highway of the cotton South, and the Union's capture of Vicksburg in 1863 split the Confederacy. Mark Twain, once a steamboat pilot, made the river famous in Life on the Mississippi and Huckleberry Finn.
